comment: Maps a displaceR binary version label to a published release asset.
The authoritative identity of a build is upstream_sha, not the DISPLACE
version string: include/version.h hardcodes VERSION and is not derived from
git tags, so many different upstream commits all report '1.6.6'.
Entries are added by hand from the step summary of the 'Build DISPLACE
binary' workflow. Bump 'default' only once a build has been smoke-tested;
users who pinned an older version keep working.
'builds' maps a glibc target to an asset. install_displace() picks the
newest build whose glibc requirement is <= the host's glibc.
'versions' is empty until the first release asset is published. Until then
install_displace() will tell the user to point DISPLACE_BINARY at a local
build, or to run the build workflow. See docs/roadmap.md.

note: Upstream 1.9.5: HEAD e454852e, commit 'v1.9.5', not tagged. The manifest default
since 2026-10-27. No feature patches. New since 1.9.3: dyn_alloc options
catch_rate_by_row and trip_time_cap (reads vessels_max_trip_hours.dat), and a fix
for N leaking from size groups that start empty.
Upstream 1.9.3: HEAD 7cf6378e, commit 'v1.9.3', not tagged. The manifest default
2026-10-14 to 2026-10-27. No feature patches: upstream ships grounds_by_port,
out_of_range_implicit, partial_fishing, seeded shuffles and the A*/do_sample fixes
itself, and the 1 h time budget is on by default (old_timestep_accounting turns it
off), so vmslike is segmented (11 columns). shortest_paths is not available.
Results differ from every 1.8.0 build.

1.8.0-96eadecb-westcoast.feature_patches: grounds-by-port headless-ipc-lazy keep-unselected-othland out-of-range-implicit astar-speedup sample-table-cache shortest-paths
note: Upstream v1.8.0 plus the displaceR feature patches used by the westcoast
analysis (docs/displace-patches.md). astar-speedup and sample-table-cache
change no output (verified byte for byte on macOS and on sequoia) and make a
run ~10-15x faster. grounds-by-port, out-of-range-implicit and shortest-paths
act only when the scenario sets their dyn_alloc option; keep-unselected-othland
changes results whenever other landings are used.
Same results as the earlier local westcoast builds, only faster.

1.8.0-96eadecb-westcoast-repro.feature_patches: grounds-by-port headless-ipc-lazy keep-unselected-othland out-of-range-implicit astar-speedup sample-table-cache shortest-paths reproducible-diffusion
note: Upstream v1.8.0 plus the displaceR feature patches used by the westcoast
analysis (docs/displace-patches.md). astar-speedup and sample-table-cache
change no output (verified byte for byte on macOS and on sequoia) and make a
run ~10-15x faster. grounds-by-port, out-of-range-implicit and shortest-paths
act only when the scenario sets their dyn_alloc option; keep-unselected-othland
changes results whenever other landings are used.
Plus reproducible-diffusion: diffusePopN draws follow the simulation
name, so two runs with the same name repeat (except upstream issue 20).
Results differ from builds without it whenever diffusePopN is used.

1.8.0-96eadecb-westcoast-timestep.feature_patches: grounds-by-port headless-ipc-lazy keep-unselected-othland out-of-range-implicit astar-speedup sample-table-cache shortest-paths reproducible-diffusion timestep-accounting
note: 1.8.0-96eadecb-westcoast-repro plus the timestep-accounting patch
(docs/timestep-accounting.md). Its dyn_alloc options timestep_accounting and
partial_fishing are off unless the scenario sets them; with them off the outputs
are byte-identical to westcoast-repro (smoke test on sequoia, 2026-10-12; only
memstats differs). With timestep_accounting on, each 1 h step is a time budget
spent on several actions, moves charge exactly the time and distance covered,
and vmslike has one row per segment with 3 more columns (seg hours km).
Upstream tag v1.8.0; the manifest default since 2026-09-23. Model behaviour
differs from 1.6.6 (N depletion, cpue multiplier, area closures, TAC
logic), so results are not comparable across the two. Built with the
ices-optional patch: a missing coord<N>_with_icesrectanglecode.dat no longer
aborts the load. All payloads bundle their third-party libraries; the Windows one also ships the MSVC runtime and carries the windows-outdir patch.
Upstream 1.6.6 was never tagged or released: 7f2656fb is v1.6.5
(45f44168) plus 8cda73cc ('v1.6.6 - Fix double counting in nodes
cumcatches', which bumps version.h) and an HPC compile fix.
Same upstream commit as 1.6.6-7f2656fb. The difference is the payload:
this build bundles Boost, GeographicLib and sqlite3 alongside the
binary. 1.6.6-7f2656fb assumed those were present on the host and fails
at startup on a server without the -dev packages installed.
The macOS build is carried over unchanged -- bundling is Linux-only.
